feeds.title: Allotment Haven
feeds.description: A quintessential British allotment in the heart of a rural English village, overgrown with pumpkins and sprinkled with bunting. Welcome to my allotment blog where I share the growing year of Plot 5 and 11W. My blog contains articles, guides, and resources for people who are interested in starting their own allotment gardens, as well as tips and advice for those who are already involved in this activity. Topics include plotting of land, choosing and growing a variety of vegetables and other plants, managing pests and other challenges, and harvesting.

feeds.title: Allotment Garden Diary
feeds.description: I'm John Harrison and grow veg, fruit, and herbs, keep poultry, write books, and run the site Allotment Gardening. Quite simply this is a record of our successes and failures growing our own fruit and vegetables, gardening, and trying to live the good life.

feeds.title: Our Plot at Green Lane Allotments
feeds.description: Our Plot at Green Lane Allotments blog is about The ups and downs of gardening on an allotment plot and garden. Also about creatures that share our gardening spaces and planet in general with us. As I'm not just a gardener sometimes my posts will stray into non-garden-related areas, and much more.

feeds.title: Flighty's plot
feeds.description: Flighty's plot is a personal blog about gardening, nature, and related topics. The author of the blog loves sharing their experiences and insights on topics such as gardening, composting, and wildlife conservation, as well as other aspects of nature that they find interesting or important.

feeds.title: The Allotment Garden
feeds.description: This blog is not just intended for those of us lucky enough to have a garden or an allotment plot; there will be plenty of tutorials, recommended garden/patio gems, and discussion points to keep you coming back for more.

feeds.title: Garden and Allotment Blog
feeds.description: Welcome to our Garden and Allotment blog. Here we provide all our best gardening blogs. We share our blogs daily so make sure you turn the notifications on.

feeds.title: Roding Road Allotments Blog
feeds.description: Roding Road Allotments Association is a community group based in London, UK, that manages a local allotment site. Follow Roding Road Allotments Blogits and know about their history, rules and regulations, events, and news. It also provides resources and advice for allotment holders, such as gardening tips, seasonal planting guides, and information about pests and diseases.

feeds.title: Plot 7 Marsh Lane
feeds.description: The Plot 7 Marsh Lane blog is a personal gardening blog written by an individual or group of people who are cultivating a plot of land in England. The blog documents the progress of the garden, providing updates on the plants, vegetables, and flowers being grown.

feeds.title: Old Lane Allotment Association Blog
feeds.description: Old Lane Allotment Association Blog is a friendly, locally-managed allotment in Beeston, Leeds. Their blog shares information about farming, daily updates, useful tips, and guidelines for farming.

feeds.title: The Green Fingered Blog
feeds.description: The Green Fingered Blog is full of ideas, advice, and inspiration for anyone who wants to get more into gardening, farming. The blog shares Simple gardening ideas to help you make the most of your outdoor space, from a huge plot to a few pots.

feeds.title: The Dorothy Parkes Centre Blog » Allotment
feeds.description: A place of welcome and opportunity for the local residents of Smethwick and the wider community. Community Centre based in Smethwick providing a range of events, activities and support services for the local community

feeds.title: Carrot Tops Allotment Blog
feeds.description: An Allotment blog exploring gardening and growing your own produce. The author of the blog shares their experiences and insights on topics such as preparing and maintaining an allotment garden, growing a variety of fruits and vegetables and composting.

feeds.title: Clairesallotment's Blog
feeds.description: Friendly gardening and allotment advice from blogger and author Claire Burgess. Sharing simple and easy gardening and allotment hints, tips and triumphs with videos and regular blog updates.

feeds.title: Mal's Edinburgh Allotment
feeds.description: Mal's Edinburgh Allotment is a personal blog about the author's experiences with allotment gardening. The author of the blog tells about their personal journey of starting and maintaining their own allotment garden, as well as tips and advice for others who are interested in doing the same.

feeds.title: Life at No.27 Blog
feeds.description: Gardening and Wellbeing Therapy Organisation. Founded in 2019, supporting children and adults. Life at No.27 is a non-profit gardening and wellbeing therapy organisation. We provide practical group and 1-2-1 classes and workshops for all ages.

feeds.title: Robs Allotment Blog
feeds.description: Robs Allotment Blog is managed by a Garden Writer based in the UK; specializing in Growing your own Garden, useful advice, vegetables, and how to get the most from your veg garden or allotment.

feeds.title: The Pink Shed
feeds.description: An allotment gardening blog following Emma's journey as she grows her own fruit and vegetables, battles weeds, builds incredibly unsafe structures and attempts to overcome her fear of nature.

feeds.title: The Good Allotment Life Blog
feeds.description: We love to grow our own so we set up this new allotment and gardening website for people who grow your own fruit and vegetables and are looking to share their experiences as gardeners. Established in 2021, we have been running our blog since then with the help of our guest bloggers. We want to publish how-to tips, successes, and failures that will be helpful to all gardeners.

feeds.title: All About Allotments
feeds.description: Brian Sheridan has an allotment in Edgbaston and is a competitive grower. Brian is also a keen photographer and loves cooking. Brian and his wife Mary will also be running a stall at Edgebaston artisan market this year, selling products made from the allotment, including his award-winning relish!This site was created to help allotment growers produce better yields and maximize the use of their space.We are currently in the stages of producing downloadable allotment plans, stay tuned!

feeds.title: The Little Allotment Company Blog
feeds.description: Hi! I'm Louise, owner and creator of The Little Allotment Company. When I'm not picking out new seed varieties or packing up orders, you'll find me up at the Allotment, pottering about with my 4-year-old daughter Savannah and our beautiful dachshund Honey. Here at The Little Allotment Company, we are passionate about providing you with high-quality, beautiful products that don't negatively impact our environment.

feeds.title: Veg Plotting
feeds.description: Award winning garden blog spiced with food, fun, travel and life in Chippenham, Wiltshire. Warning: there may be cats and cake. Enjoy!

feeds.title: Real Men Sow Blog
feeds.description: Hello I'm Pete and I'm currently based in the west of Scotland, in a small place called Rosneath, where I'm exploring my garden adventures. I personally started gardening around 6 years ago and initially, I started out by growing my favorite fruits and berries, such as strawberries, Raspberries & Gooseberries. Since then I've added a lot of vegetables and working closely with my neighbor, it's been a lot of fun. Head straight to my blog and learn ore about me, my farms, the things I grow, the entire process of farming and more useful stuff dor you.

feeds.title: Lovely Greens
feeds.description: The Lovely Greens blog shares Natural soap making recipes and organic gardening tips from Tanya Anderson of Lovely Greens. Live Simply, Grow Your Own, Make Natural Things.

feeds.title: Humber Ave Allotment
feeds.description: Humber Avenue Community Allotments (HACA) was formed on the 18th of August 2021 to manage the allotments at Humber Avenue on behalf of Worthing Borough Council (WBC) following a vote for self-management. Their mission is to provide environmentally sustainable allotments for cultivation through a non-profit making social enterprise for the local community which promotes inclusivity and diversity. Follow their bloga and learn more about the Humber community, their work, past projects, and useful articles on farming and gardening.

feeds.title: The National Allotment Society
feeds.description: The National Allotment Society (NAS) is the leading national organisation upholding the interests and rights of the allotment community across the UK. We work with government at national and local levels, other organisations and landlords to provide, promote and preserve allotments for all. We offer support, guidance and advice to our members and those with an interest in allotment gardening.
